text: SS Olympia was a steamship that operated in the northwest United States and Alaska during the Klondike Gold Rush and was wrecked in 1910. Originally laid down as SS Doune Castle, she was launched in 1883 as SS Dunbar Castle by Barclay, Curle and Co. of Glasgow, Scotland, for the Castle Mail Packet Company. In 1895, Dunbar Castle was sold to Fairfield Ship Building and Engineering Co. and renamed SS Olympia. In 1897, the Scottish American Steamship Company purchased her, and later that year, the Northern Pacific Steamship Line acquired her. In 1898, she operated under the North America Mail Steamship Company of Tacoma, Washington. In 1903, she served with the North Western Steam Ship Company of Seattle, Washington, which sold her to the Alaska Steam Ship Company in 1904; that year, lifeboats were installed. On 10 December 1910, Olympia ran aground on Bligh Reef off Alaska's Prince William Sound and sank, with no loss of life. After the incident, steamboat inspectors accused Captain Daniels, who was in command at the time of the grounding, of "unskillful navigation." The coordinates of the wreck site are 60°50′26″N 146°52′48″W (60.840529°N 146.880015°W).
